name: Copper Processing
description: Turn copper into machine parts and use mechanical power to improve ore yield.

pages.text: $(bold)From metal to machinery$()$(br2)The Copper Age starts by turning your first ingots into manufactured parts. The Primitive Anvil makes Copper Plates, and the Mechanical Grinder is the first machine that rewards building a working rotational network.

pages.title: Primitive Anvil
pages.text: Right-click the anvil with a Copper Ingot, then strike it four times with the Primitive Hammer. The workpiece is shown on the anvil and becomes a Copper Plate after the final strike.

$(bold)Copper Plates$()$(br2)Copper Plates reinforce many Copper Age mechanisms: control blocks, protection devices, the brake and the crank all build on this first metalworking step.$(br2)Use an empty hand on the completed anvil workpiece to pick it up.

pages.title: Mechanical Grinder
pages.text: Place the Mechanical Grinder Base and put the Grinder Stone directly above it, then right-click the base to form the two-block machine.

pages.name: Mechanical Grinder
pages.text: The Grinder Stone sits directly above the base. Mechanical input is on the LEFT side of the stone base. Place a horizontal Wooden Shaft against the visible bearing. The grinder requires at least 20 mechanical speed and 4 torque.

$(bold)Crushing Chalcocite$()$(br2)Right-click the formed grinder with Chalcocite Ore. With at least 20 speed and 4 torque it runs for about eight seconds and produces Crushed Chalcocite.$(br2)If the drivetrain stops, processing pauses rather than losing progress. Use an empty hand to retrieve output.

$(bold)Why crush it?$()$(br2)Direct Primitive Furnace processing remains valid: one Chalcocite Ore gives one Copper Ingot plus Slag.$(br2)Crushing first improves the same furnace batch to $(bold)two Copper Ingots$() plus Slag. Your mechanical workshop therefore improves resource efficiency instead of existing only as a progression lock.

pages.title: Mechanical Ore Washer
pages.text: The Ore Washer is a rotary trommel for crushed ore. Give its shaft at least the recipe's required speed/torque and keep a water source directly adjacent. The drum separates lighter gangue while producing a cleaner washed mineral.

$(bold)Washer rules$()$(br2)The Washer is a real Gear V2 shaft node, so it can sit directly in a drivetrain. Recipes define their own minimum RPM, torque, processing time and optional byproduct chance.$(br2)Empty-hand right-click removes finished output first, then byproduct, then unprocessed input. The machine also exposes an item capability for later automation.

pages.title: Mechanical Sifter
pages.text: The Sifter is driven by a Crank rather than a shaft. Place it directly on the Crank's linear-output side. The upper and lower screens shake in opposite motion and classify washed material into concentrate and optional gangue.

$(bold)Cassiterite -> Tin$()$(br2)Cassiterite now has the first complete beneficiation chain: $(br)1. Mechanical Grinder -> Crushed Cassiterite$(br)2. Ore Washer + water -> Washed Cassiterite$(br)3. Crank-driven Sifter -> Tin Concentrate$(br)4. Primitive Furnace + coal -> Tin Ingot

$(bold)First Bronze$()$(br2)Combine three Copper Ingots with one Tin Ingot to prepare a Bronze Alloy Charge. Fire the charge with coal in the Primitive Furnace to produce four Bronze Ingots.$(br2)Making the first Bronze therefore proves that the Copper workshop can mine, crush, wash, classify and smelt an alloy feedstock.

$(bold)Data-driven ore processing$()$(br2)Grinding, washing and sifting requirements now live in recipe JSON instead of being hard-coded into each machine. New minerals can define their own speed, torque, time, outputs and byproduct chance without another Java machine class.$(br2)This is the foundation for processing the rest of Magneticraft2's ore catalogue through later ages.
